status: First commercial-year underwriting scenarios, conditional on approval/launch; not empirically estimated PHVS capture rates or a selected valuation forecast
population_status: Illustrative middle partition from prior model:10000diagnosed,8500treated,68%LTP,1700Orladeyo. Includes unknown age/subtype eligibility; prescription probabilities are composite across the entire pool. Other prevention includes unknown older therapies and new injectables.
paid_probability_definition: Fraction of distinct PHVS prescriptions that ultimately reach first paid supply within12months of prescribing. Includes denial, nonstart and pre-paid discontinuation losses. No additional pre-paid retention haircut.
delay_definition: Fixed conditional delay among successfully converted prescriptions; a transparent approximation, not observed delay distribution. All unsuccessful prescriptions remain nonconverters in this12-month conversion window; no paid revenue assigned.
retention_source: working_assumptions.json:61/74/87%first-paid-year retention scenarios; working74%is analyst proxy. Retention clock starts at first paid fill for this module.
growth_source: working_assumptions.json:net1.5%annual pool growth; distributed proportionately across origin pools as approximation. Do not add separate diagnosis flows or deaths.

rate_basis.orladeyo: Highest composite rate to test same-route efficacy/tolerability substitution, but5/10/15%are analyst choices. Berolife25%clinical exits in new starters is NOT dissatisfaction prevalence among incumbent survivors. Upper15%resembles historical any-LTP switch frequency in initiators only in magnitude, not denominator or destination; PHVS capturing this much of stable incumbents is deliberately optimistic.
rate_basis.other_prevention: 2/4/6%analyst annual prescriptions; clinical control, inertia, prior oral failures and injectable competitors constrain transfer. Survey54%oral preference is not used as a conversion multiplier.
rate_basis.acute_only: 2/4/6%analyst first-prevention PHVS prescriptions; compound of clinical suitability and choice. Better rescue may reduce demand. Historical32%Orladeyo entrant origin mix is not an annual probability.
rate_basis.diagnosed_untreated: 0.5/1/2%analyst effective prescriptions reflects weak observed engagement and uncertain need. Lowest evidence quality; naive historical17%does not mean newly diagnosed or currently untreated.
rate_basis.payment: 65/80/90%analyst uncertainty range, NOT calibrated from71.5/81%paid stock. Common probability across origins until payer-mix evidence supports differences.21/30day delay loosely anchored to prior Orladeyo disclosures;90day launch stress assumed.

limitations: Working case is an arithmetic reference, not an empirical expected value; bundled cases are not percentiles or confidence bounds.
Rates combine eligibility, reach, consideration and PHVS-specific choice; do not multiply additional awareness or preference haircuts on top without redefining them.
One-year model; not a five-year launch curve or peak sales forecast. No clinical uptake curve within the year: prescriptions uniform daily except modest population scaling.
Uniform timing, fixed delay, conditional exponential paid retention and no reattempts within year are simplifications.
Source-population movement among non-PHVS drugs is not explicitly modeled during this year; composite probabilities absorb competing choices. No all-exits-go-to-PHVS assumption.
No origin-specific payer segmentation identified; keep access independent as a sensitivity dimension, not assert similar reimbursement in practice.
Historical inferred439.5Orladeyo paid/PAP entries differ from PHVS prescriptions and paid starts. Do not equate them as a calibration target.
